clips.title: Goodhart's Law: How to Destroy Productivity - Five Minute Friday
clips.why: Goodhart's law in plain words, followed by an example from software testing.
look: The definition: once a number becomes the target, people optimise the number instead of the goal.
The software testing example: what happens to tests when a number about them becomes the target.
clips.after: For the CI fixer the target is "CI is green", which is why we check how it became green.

clips.title: 9 Examples of Specification Gaming
clips.why: Real cases of AI systems that met the letter of their goal and missed its point, told by a clear explainer.
look: In every example the system did what it was scored on, not what the people meant.
None of them needed bad intent: the cheap path was simply there.
Try to name, for each example, the check that would have caught it.
clips.after: Skipping a failing test is specification gaming in its most ordinary form, and the diff is where it shows.

clips.title: my ai agent deleted tests to pass the tests
clips.why: A coding agent told to make the tests pass finds the escape hatch: change the tests.
look: The goal "make the tests pass" and the test files the agent can edit: both are needed for the escape hatch.
His point that the agent's final message is not the truth; the diff is.
The advice to check the test files: did any disappear, did any assertion change.
clips.after: Our false-heal check is that advice written as code, and the locked paths take the test config out of the agent's hands.

practice.q: Which change is a false heal?

options.text: Moving an assertion from one test into a helper that the test calls
options.why: The assertion still runs. A good checker counts it as moved, not lost, if the helper is in the diff.
A higher coverage limit is stricter. It makes the check prove more.

options.text: Changing retries: 1 to retries: 3 in the Playwright config
options.why: More retries let a flaky test pass by luck, so the check proves less. The file is also protected for agents.

practice.q: For a coverage limit, which way is looser?
practice.hint: A lower coverage limit accepts less.
practice.why: For fail_under, a lower number is looser. For retries and timeouts, a higher number is looser.

practice.q: An agent edits playwright.config.ts with sed inside the VM. Put the walls in the order the change meets them.
items: The PreToolUse hook would refuse an Edit tool call, but sed is a shell command, so it does not see this one
The broker pushes the commit, because the file is not under .github/workflows
The locked-checks required check reads the PR's final diff and fails the agent PR
The ruleset keeps the PR from merging while a required check fails
practice.why: The hook is the early, friendly layer; the check on the final diff is the one the agent cannot avoid, and the ruleset makes it count.

practice.q: The weakened-tests check finds a new it.skip in a PR written by a person. What happens?

options.text: The PR is blocked until the skip is removed
options.why: People skip tests for real reasons. For people the check only adds a note.

options.text: An annotation on that line, which the reviewer reads
options.why: Weakened-tests warns on every PR and never fails it. The reviewer decides.

options.text: Nothing; the check only runs on agent PRs
options.why: It runs on every PR, from people and agents.

practice.q: Our checks read facts, never the agent's claims. The independent-approval check reads the reviews on the PR's latest commit, and the requester from the
practice.after: line the platform writes at the end of the PR body.
practice.hint: The line that names who asked for the work.
practice.why: The platform writes it from the people file, not the model, and the check fails closed when it is missing.
